elements.name: dashboard
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This page provides an overview of all projects, displaying key metrics like total revenue, cost, and average margin. It also allows users to sort the project list.
detailedUserActions: Select a sorting option from the dropdown menu to reorder the project list.
Click on a project (implied by UButton/div actions) to view its detailed information.
conditionalStates: An "Error loading projects" alert is displayed if there's an issue fetching project data.
dataProvenance: Project summaries are fetched from an API using `useQuery` and stored in `result`.

`projectsData` is derived from `projectSummaries`, mapping each summary to detailed project information including ID, name, client, start date, estimated end date, total cost, expected revenue, net margin, and job count.
`totalRevenue` is calculated by summing the `expectedRevenue` of all projects in `projectsData`.
`totalCost` is calculated by summing the `totalCost` of all projects in `projectsData`.
`averageMargin` is calculated by summing the `netMargin` of all projects in `projectsData` and dividing by the total number of projects. If there are no projects, the average margin is 0.
`sortedProjects` are derived from `projectsData` and ordered based on the selected `sortBy` field. Dates are sorted most recent first, other fields alphabetically or numerically.
businessLogic: The `averageMarginClass` determines the color of the average margin display: green for >= 25%, yellow for >= 15%, and red for less than 15%.

Projects can be sorted by 'Name (A-Z)', 'Client (A-Z)', 'Start date (most recent)', 'Total cost (highest to lowest)', 'Expected revenue (highest to lowest)', 'Net margin (highest to lowest)', and 'Number of jobs (most to least)'.

elements.name: index
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This is the landing page of the application, providing navigation to other sections.
detailedUserActions: Click on a card (UCard) to navigate to a different section of the application.

elements.name: login
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This page allows users to log into the application using their email and password.
detailedUserActions: Enter your email address into the email input field.
Enter your password into the password input field.
Submit the form to log in.
Click the button to pre-populate the email and password fields with demo data.
conditionalStates: The button (for login or demo credentials) is disabled while the login process is in progress (loading).
businessLogic: Both email and password fields are required for login.

elements.name: index
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This page displays a list of all projects and allows users to create new projects.
detailedUserActions: Click a button (UButton) to toggle the new project form visibility.
After a project is successfully created, the project list will refresh.
dataProvenance: The project list is refreshed after a new project is created.

elements.name: new
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This page provides a dedicated form for creating a new project.

elements.name: [id]
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This page displays the detailed view of a specific project, including its jobs and financial breakdown, and allows for editing jobs or the project itself.
detailedUserActions: Click a button (UButton) to show the quote summary.
Click a button (UButton) to open a modal for adding a new job.
Click a button (UButton) to edit a specific job, which opens a slideover panel.
Click a button (UButton) to close the job editing slideover.
After a job is saved, the slideover closes and the project data is refreshed.
After a new job is created, the add job modal closes and the project data is refreshed.
Click a button (UButton) to open a modal for editing the project details.
After project details are saved, the edit project modal closes and the project data is refreshed.
conditionalStates: Buttons related to jobs are disabled if the project has no jobs.
A slideover panel (`USlideover`) is used to edit jobs, which opens and closes based on user actions.
dataProvenance: The project ID is extracted from the route parameters.
The `activeJob` is found within the project's jobs based on `activeJobId`.
Project data is refreshed after jobs or project details are saved.
businessLogic: The `id` of the project is derived from the URL parameter and converted to a number.
The `activeJob` is identified by matching its ID with the `activeJobId`.

elements.name: app
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This is the root component of the application, responsible for setting up the main layout and rendering pages.

elements.name: ArkHeader
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This component provides the application's header, including the brand name, theme toggle, and user information with a logout option.
detailedUserActions: Click the "Logout" button to sign out of the application.
Click the theme toggle (ThemeToggle component) to switch between light and dark modes.
dataProvenance: User display name is derived from the current user's employee name, username, or email.
User role is mapped from technical role names (e.g., 'ADMIN' to 'Administrator').
businessLogic: The `getUserDisplayName` function prioritizes displaying the employee name, then username, then email for the current user.
The `getUserRole` function maps internal role codes (e.g., 'ADMIN') to more user-friendly labels (e.g., 'Administrator').

elements.name: AddJobForm
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This form allows users to add a new job to a specific project, including details like title, category, complexity, price, and assigned employee.
detailedUserActions: Fill in the 'title' field for the job.
Select a 'category' for the job.
Enter the 'estimatedComplexity' for the job.
Enter the 'price' for the job.
Optionally, select an 'assignedEmployeeId' for the job.
Submit the form to create the job.
Click a button (UButton) to cancel or close the form.
conditionalStates: Form fields are validated as the user interacts with them, showing error messages for invalid input.
The submit button is disabled if the form is invalid or currently submitting.
dataProvenance: The `projectId` is passed as a prop to associate the job with a project.
`currentJobs` are derived from the project's existing jobs.
`availableEmployees` are filtered from all employees, considering their availability and ensuring the currently assigned employee (if any) is included.
businessLogic: Title is required, must be between 3 and 100 characters.
Category is required and must be one of 'ELECTRICAL', 'PLUMBING', 'CARPENTRY', 'PAINTING', 'OTHER'.
Estimated complexity and price are required and must be positive numbers.
The form is considered valid only if all required fields are filled and there are no validation errors.
Upon successful job creation, a toast notification is displayed.

elements.name: JobForm
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This form is used to edit an existing job's details, including its title, estimated complexity, price, and assigned employee. It also calculates the estimated job cost.
detailedUserActions: Enter or update the "Job title" in the input field.
Adjust the estimated complexity and price.
Select an employee from the dropdown to assign or reassign the job.
Click a button (UButton) to confirm an employee reassignment.
Click a button (UButton) to cancel an employee reassignment.
Click a button (UButton) to reset the form fields to their initial state.
Submit the form to save the updated job details.
visibleElements: "Job title" input field (UInput) with placeholder "Job title"
conditionalStates: The assigned employee dropdown is disabled while employee data is loading.
Individual employee options in the dropdown are disabled if the employee is not available.
The submit button is disabled while the form is submitting or if the form is invalid.
A confirmation dialog appears if an employee is being reassigned.
dataProvenance: The `jobId` and `projectId` are passed as props to identify the job and its project.
`currentJobs` are derived from the project's jobs.
`employeeOptions` are generated from available employees, including their roles, hourly costs, and availability.
`selectedEmployeeDetails` are derived from the chosen employee in the dropdown, including their name, role, hourly cost, and productivity.
`estimatedJobCost` is calculated based on the job's `estimatedComplexity`, the `selectedEmployeeDetails`'s `hourlyCost`, and `productivity`.
businessLogic: Form fields are validated against a schema, and error messages are displayed for invalid input.
The form is considered valid (`isValid`) if all required fields are filled and there are no validation errors.
If an employee is reassigned, a confirmation dialog is shown before the change is applied.
The estimated job cost is calculated as `(estimatedComplexity / employeeProductivity) * employeeHourlyRate`.
Required fields for validation include 'title', 'estimatedComplexity', 'price', and 'assignedEmployeeId'.

elements.name: CostBreakdownCard
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This component displays a summary of a project's financial metrics, including total cost, expected revenue, and net margin.
dataProvenance: All financial data (jobs, total cost, expected revenue, net margin) is passed as a `project` prop.
`jobs`, `totalCost`, `expectedRevenue`, and `netMargin` are directly derived from the `project` prop.

elements.name: EditProjectForm
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This form allows users to edit the details of an existing project, such as its name, client, start date, and estimated end date.
detailedUserActions: Enter or update the project's name in the input field (placeholder: "Ex: Kitchen renovation").
Enter or update the client's name in the input field (placeholder: "Ex: John Doe").
Select or update the project's start date.
Select or update the project's estimated end date.
Submit the form to save the updated project details.
Click a button (UButton) to cancel or close the form.
visibleElements: Project name input field (UInput) with placeholder "Ex: Kitchen renovation"
Client name input field (UInput) with placeholder "Ex: John Doe"
conditionalStates: The save button is disabled while the form is submitting (loading).
The save button is disabled if the form is invalid.
Form fields are validated as the user interacts with them, showing error messages for invalid input.
dataProvenance: The `project` object and `projectId` are passed as props to pre-fill and identify the project being edited.
businessLogic: Project name is required, must be between 3 and 100 characters.
Client name is required, must be between 2 and 100 characters.
Start date and estimated end date are required.
The form is considered valid (`isFormValid`) if all required fields are filled and there are no validation errors.
Upon successful project update, a toast notification is displayed.

elements.name: ProjectForm
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This form allows users to create a new project by providing its name, client, start date, and estimated end date.
detailedUserActions: Enter the project's name in the input field.
Enter the client's name in the input field.
Select the project's start date (defaults to today).
Select the project's estimated end date.
Submit the form to create the new project.
conditionalStates: Form fields are validated as the user interacts with them, showing error messages for invalid input.
The create project button is disabled if the form is invalid or currently submitting.
businessLogic: Project name is required, must be between 3 and 100 characters.
Client name is required, must be between 2 and 100 characters.
Start date and estimated end date are required.
The start date defaults to the current day.
The estimated end date must be on or after the start date.
The form is considered valid (`isFormValid`) if all required fields are filled and there are no validation errors.
Upon successful project creation, a toast notification is displayed.

elements.name: ProjectHeader
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This component displays the header for a project, including its name, client, and key dates, with an optional edit button.
detailedUserActions: Click the edit button (UButton) to modify project details.
conditionalStates: An edit button is shown if `showEditButton` prop is true.
dataProvenance: All project details (name, client, dates) are passed as a `project` prop.
businessLogic: Dates are formatted for display (e.g., 'Jan 1, 2023').

elements.name: QuoteSummary
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This component generates and displays a detailed summary of a project's quote, including job counts, total hours, costs, revenue, and margin, with options to print or share.
detailedUserActions: Click a button (UButton) to print the quote summary.
Click a button (UButton) to share the quote summary via native sharing options or copy to clipboard.
Click a button (UButton) to close the summary view.
dataProvenance: All project and job details are passed as a `project` prop.
`totalJobs` is the count of jobs in the project.
`totalHours` is the sum of `estimatedComplexity` for all jobs.
`totalCost` is the sum of `price` for all jobs.
`netMargin` is calculated as `expectedRevenue - totalCost`.
`netMarginPercentage` is calculated as `(netMargin / expectedRevenue) * 100`.
businessLogic: Dates are formatted for display.
Job categories are mapped from technical codes to user-friendly labels (e.g., 'ELECTRICAL' to 'Electrical').
The `printSummary` function opens a new window and prints the content of the quote summary.
The `shareSummary` function attempts to use the browser's native share API; if unavailable, it copies the summary text to the clipboard.

elements.name: ThemeToggle
elements.summaryDescriptionInLaymansTerms: This component allows users to switch between different visual themes (e.g., light and dark mode) for the application.
detailedUserActions: Click the button to toggle the application's theme.
